en.choice.boxing-muro.title: The wall of names
en.choice.boxing-muro.text: Before your first training session, Gorin leads you into the locker room. Dozens of photographs hang on the wall: his pupils, one by one. Almost every face has been crossed out with red marker. One photo, at the back, has been turned to face the wall.
en.choice.boxing-muro.a.label: You ask who the turned photo is
en.choice.boxing-muro.a.text: Gorin hesitates, then says a single name: “Idris”. It isn't a memory he wanted to share, but he thanks you for not looking away.
en.choice.boxing-muro.b.label: You promise him your face will never end up on that wall
en.choice.boxing-muro.b.text: “Don't promise what isn't yours to decide,” says Gorin. But for a moment his gaze softens, and he squeezes your shoulder hard.
en.choice.boxing-muro.c.label: You say your name will hang higher than any of them
en.choice.boxing-muro.c.text: Gorin barely smiles. It is the smile of a man who has heard those words before, and never liked how they ended.
en.choice.boxing-cronista.title: The reporter's notebook
en.choice.boxing-cronista.text: After your first fight your name has already gone round the alleys. A girl with a recorder is waiting outside the gym: her name is Lia Marek and she writes for a neighbourhood paper. “Ten minutes,” she says. “Tell me how it really went.”
en.choice.boxing-cronista.a.label: You tell her the truth, Gorin's gym included
en.choice.boxing-cronista.a.text: Lia writes in silence and never interrupts. The article will run with a photo of the gym: for Gorin, the first good publicity in years.
en.choice.boxing-cronista.b.label: You embellish the facts a little: a good story makes news
en.choice.boxing-cronista.b.text: “Three rounds? Six,” she smiles, and writes six. The headline is huge, and tomorrow someone will recognise you in the street. You're left with the doubt that someone knows how it really went.
en.choice.boxing-cronista.c.label: You walk past without answering
en.choice.boxing-cronista.c.text: Lia watches you walk away. She doesn't push, but she closes the notebook so slowly it feels like a promise: you'll see her again.
en.choice.boxing-manager.title: The champion's manager
en.choice.boxing-manager.text: Half an hour before you step into the ring against the regional champion, a man in a shiny jacket takes you aside. He is the champion's manager and he speaks softly: “My boy has a knee that can't hold any more. A little push to the ankle in round two and the title is yours. Nobody will ever know.”
en.choice.boxing-manager.extra0.text: At the end of the corridor you spot Lia Marek with her notebook open. She doesn't seem to be listening, but she hasn't taken her eyes off you.
en.choice.boxing-manager.a.label: You accept: one low blow and the title is yours
en.choice.boxing-manager.a.text: You shake his hand without looking at him. It's easy, far too easy: the champion is slower before the bell even rings. But something shifts inside you and never quite settles back.
en.choice.boxing-manager.b.label: You refuse and warn the champion yourself
en.choice.boxing-manager.b.text: The champion studies you for a long time. “Strange way to start a fight,” he says, and for the first time someone in the ring shakes your hand before the bell.
en.choice.boxing-manager.c.label: You refuse and expose him in front of everyone
en.choice.boxing-manager.c.text: The hall falls silent. The manager is escorted out amid whistles and your name bounces from mouth to mouth: honest or showy, depending on who says it.
en.choice.boxing-ginocchio.title: The knee and the old man
en.choice.boxing-ginocchio.text: Your knee sends a stab of pain, and Gorin notices before you can even try to hide it. “The heavyweight will eat you for breakfast,” he says. “I can stop you. Tonight.” Then, lower: “Idris had that same look the day a man in black came looking for him.”
en.choice.boxing-ginocchio.extra0.text: So the face turned to the wall had a name, and now it has a story too.
en.choice.boxing-ginocchio.a.label: You grit your teeth: that was never the point
en.choice.boxing-ginocchio.a.text: Gorin doesn't argue. He wraps your knee in silence, tightly, and doesn't look you in the face.
en.choice.boxing-ginocchio.b.label: You accept his care and his judgement
en.choice.boxing-ginocchio.b.text: You rest until the pain eases. Losing an hour no longer feels like surrender: it feels like understanding something nobody ever taught Idris.
en.choice.boxing-ginocchio.c.label: You ask him to tell you everything about Idris and the man in black
en.choice.boxing-ginocchio.c.text: Gorin talks until the ice melts. He tells you about contracts, struck-out names, a boy who climbed and never came back down. You leave the locker room knowing what you are climbing against.
en.choice.boxing-uomo-in-nero.title: The man in black
en.choice.boxing-uomo-in-nero.text: In the corridor of the arena, minutes before the fight with the Legend, the man in black waits leaning against the wall. His notebook is open at the page with your name already written. “Winning isn't necessary,” he says quietly. “Being remembered is. I take care of that. All it takes is a signature.”
en.choice.boxing-uomo-in-nero.extra0.text: At the far end of the corridor Gorin watches you, motionless, your wraps still in his hands.
en.choice.boxing-uomo-in-nero.extra1.text: Gorin isn't at the far end of the corridor: he said he wouldn't come to watch.
en.choice.boxing-uomo-in-nero.extra2.text: He knows about the low blow. He mentions it with a half smile, as if it were a mark of merit.
en.choice.boxing-uomo-in-nero.a.label: You sign: your name goes in the Registry
en.choice.boxing-uomo-in-nero.a.text: The pen glides over the paper with suspicious ease. “Excellent,” he says. “From now on nobody will be able to say they don't know you.”
en.choice.boxing-uomo-in-nero.b.label: You don't sign, but ask what he really writes
en.choice.boxing-uomo-in-nero.b.text: He smiles, almost pleased. “That's the right question.” He doesn't answer, but lets the notebook slip for a moment: before he snaps it shut, you have time to read another line, and then another.
en.choice.boxing-uomo-in-nero.c.label: You ignore him and go to fight
en.choice.boxing-uomo-in-nero.c.text: You walk past him without stopping. Behind you, you hear only the sound of a pen that keeps writing anyway.
en.choice.battlefield-lista.title: The camp roster
en.choice.battlefield-lista.text: Sergeant Vance hands you a cot and a pen. “Name and speciality for the camp roster. Everyone has one here: you fist-fighters usually write 'endurance'.”
en.choice.battlefield-lista.extra0.text: Your name is already on the roster, in a handwriting you recognise.
en.choice.battlefield-lista.extra1.text: Your name isn't on any list, and Vance doesn't like names he doesn't know.
en.choice.battlefield-lista.extra2.text: Someone in line whispers that you won 'with some help'. Rumours cross the sea faster than ships.
en.choice.battlefield-lista.a.label: You write your name, nothing more
en.choice.battlefield-lista.a.text: Vance reads the line and nods. “One who doesn't sell himself. Rare around here, and I don't know yet if that's a good thing.”
en.choice.battlefield-lista.b.label: You write your ring name and your victories
en.choice.battlefield-lista.b.text: Vance raises an eyebrow, but word spreads: the kid from the ring has arrived. Some greet you, some size you up.
en.choice.battlefield-lista.c.label: You ask for the toughest tests
en.choice.battlefield-lista.c.text: “As you wish,” says Vance, and gives you the heaviest shift in camp. A hunger like that doesn't go unnoticed, neither by him nor by whoever watches from above.
en.choice.battlefield-ferito.title: Under the sniper's line
en.choice.battlefield-ferito.text: The sniper has already seen you, but he isn't shooting at you. Twenty metres away, behind a wreck, a recruit lies pinned with a wounded leg. One movement is enough to trigger the next shot. The sniper waits: he wants to see what you'll do.
en.choice.battlefield-ferito.a.label: You crawl to him and drag him to cover
en.choice.battlefield-ferito.a.text: The bullet grazes your back twice, but you get him behind the wall. The boy grips your wrist: “I won't forget who you are.” You didn't need it, but it warms you.
en.choice.battlefield-ferito.b.label: You use him as a decoy to cross the line
en.choice.battlefield-ferito.b.text: You cross while the sniper shoots at the boy, and the blast covers the rest. Behind you nobody calls your name, and for a while you wouldn't want to hear it.
en.choice.battlefield-ferito.c.label: You radio the position and wait for rescue
en.choice.battlefield-ferito.c.text: For twenty minutes nothing happens. Then the medics arrive with a smoke bomb and carry the boy off without thanking you: the credit isn't yours, but neither is the blame.
en.choice.battlefield-idris.title: Idris's hand
en.choice.battlefield-idris.text: At the armoury, while the armourers laugh at your bare fists, a soldier with a cybernetic left arm stops in front of you. He has the face you saw turned to the wall, aged ten years. “So you're Gorin's pupil,” he says. “I'm Idris. If you want to get to the end, you should know what I learned.”
en.choice.battlefield-idris.extra0.text: He looks at the wraps Gorin gave you with something like regret.
en.choice.battlefield-idris.extra1.text: You already know what that steel arm hides: a contract he has never finished paying off.
en.choice.battlefield-idris.a.label: You take his hand and his advice
en.choice.battlefield-idris.a.text: Idris shows you a few shortcuts Gorin would never have taught you. They work. You use them with a pinch of shame and an excellent reason not to stop.
en.choice.battlefield-idris.b.label: You challenge him: Gorin never taught you to obey
en.choice.battlefield-idris.b.text: Idris laughs, at last. “Then prove it when we climb.” He turns his back with a curt nod: not a friendship, but a bet between two lonely people.
en.choice.battlefield-idris.c.label: You ask why he left Gorin
en.choice.battlefield-idris.c.text: Idris doesn't answer at once. “Because stopping at that level was like growing old in a cage.” Then, almost voiceless: “And because he was right, and I didn't want to hear it.”
en.choice.battlefield-pilota.title: The pilot who feels no pain
en.choice.battlefield-pilota.text: The ground trembles. The war mech waiting for you has a pilot command only mentions in low voices: a former soldier who had every nerve switched off to avoid feeling anything at all. At the briefing they let you choose how to prepare.
en.choice.battlefield-pilota.extra0.text: At the back of the line, the boy you saved gives you a small military salute.
en.choice.battlefield-pilota.extra1.text: At the back of the line, someone avoids your eyes with far too much care.
en.choice.battlefield-pilota.a.label: You ask to speak with him before the fight
en.choice.battlefield-pilota.a.text: Behind the glass is a tired man who asks you, almost in a whisper, not to kill him. When you come out, nobody asks what you said to each other.
en.choice.battlefield-pilota.b.label: You offer command a report on your comrades' weak points
en.choice.battlefield-pilota.b.text: The general reads the report with almost affectionate attention. “A good tool knows how to recognise other tools,” he says. It isn't a compliment.
en.choice.battlefield-pilota.c.label: You study the mech from afar and do nothing else
en.choice.battlefield-pilota.c.text: You spend the night watching how it moves, how it loses a beat every third step. You tell nobody: it seems the most honest way not to get it wrong.
en.choice.battlefield-sigillo.title: The general's seal
en.choice.battlefield-sigillo.text: In the bunker, before facing the general, you find a crate bearing his seal. Inside are hundreds of sheets: the names of everyone who has climbed this far, one by one, each with a date and a short note. On the oldest ones, always the same word: “consumed”. The last line, at the bottom, is for you.
en.choice.battlefield-sigillo.extra0.text: Idris's name appears three times, each time with a different figure beside it. You realise it isn't a contract: it's a debt.
en.choice.battlefield-sigillo.extra1.text: Idris's name is circled in pencil. Beside it, a single word: “to be surpassed”.
en.choice.battlefield-sigillo.a.label: You burn the pages without reading further
en.choice.battlefield-sigillo.a.text: The fire takes well. For a moment you feel a weight leave the bunker, and you understand that nobody can use those names against anyone again. Not even against you.
en.choice.battlefield-sigillo.b.label: You keep the list: it may serve as leverage
en.choice.battlefield-sigillo.b.text: You slip it inside your jacket. It weighs more than it should. You think that one day you'll look the man in black in the eye with something in your hand.
en.choice.battlefield-sigillo.c.label: You show it to the soldiers: they have to know
en.choice.battlefield-sigillo.c.text: The mess falls silent. Then someone starts reading aloud. Within an hour the word has run through the whole camp, and your name with it.
en.choice.battlefield-sigillo.c.lock: Nobody would listen to a name they don't know: you need more Fame.
en.choice.desert-acqua.title: Water for two days
en.choice.desert-acqua.text: You have water for two days and no map. Behind a dune, a caravan has stopped: Nuhra, the guide, has cracked lips and a dozen people behind her. A raider has been trailing you all for hours, sure that thirst will do the work for him.
en.choice.desert-acqua.extra0.text: Among the travellers you think you recognise a camp uniform, and you lower your eyes.
en.choice.desert-acqua.extra1.text: Some of them have heard about the list: they look at you the way one looks at a witness.
en.choice.desert-acqua.a.label: You share your water with the whole caravan
en.choice.desert-acqua.a.text: Your flask lasts less than half a day. Nuhra shakes your hand without a word and draws a line in the sand: the shortest way to the oasis.
en.choice.desert-acqua.b.label: You trade your name for water: “I'm the one from the Ring”
en.choice.desert-acqua.b.text: The story of the boxer who crossed the sea is worth more than a flask. Nuhra laughs, refills your supply and will tell of you at every well.
en.choice.desert-acqua.c.label: You press on alone without stopping
en.choice.desert-acqua.c.text: You save water and strength. Behind you, for a while, you hear footsteps stop. You don't turn round.
en.choice.desert-lettera.title: Gorin's letter
en.choice.desert-lettera.text: An exhausted rider reaches you at the well with a parcel wrapped in waxed cloth. Inside, a pair of old wraps and a sheet with three handwritten lines: “The knee? Remember to breathe. The gym holds. Come back whenever you like.”
en.choice.desert-lettera.a.label: You reply at once and promise to return
en.choice.desert-lettera.a.text: You write on a torn sheet, sand between your fingers. The rider leaves at dawn: Gorin, at least, will know his pupil remembers.
en.choice.desert-lettera.b.label: You keep it without replying
en.choice.desert-lettera.b.text: You tuck it into your pack along with the wraps. It isn't a lack of affection: replying would mean stopping, and you can't.
en.choice.desert-lettera.c.label: You burn it: now is not the time
en.choice.desert-lettera.c.text: The sheet burns in seconds, and with it your only excuse to turn back. The rider doesn't look at you: he has seen others do it.
en.choice.desert-voci.title: Voices from the well
en.choice.desert-voci.text: At the well a merchant shares news from across the sea: a suburban gym has closed over debts and the old man who ran it now sleeps in the ring, among the bags. He says Gorin's name as if it were a wrong address.
en.choice.desert-voci.a.label: You entrust him with half your winnings for Gorin
en.choice.desert-voci.a.text: The merchant counts the coins with an unreadable expression, then wraps them in a cloth. “If I lose them, you'll know,” he says. Not a guarantee, but a start.
en.choice.desert-voci.b.label: You tell everyone at the well about the gym
en.choice.desert-voci.b.text: The story of a gym holding on without money works better than an advert. By evening, three caravans are talking about it, and your name is in every version.
en.choice.desert-voci.c.label: You say it no longer concerns you
en.choice.desert-voci.c.text: The merchant nods without judging you. Later, alone, you notice you've repeated the phrase three times and none of them rang true.
en.choice.desert-rito.title: The mummy's rite
en.choice.desert-rito.text: Among the ruins of a buried temple, the Mummy Warrior doesn't attack you: she hands you a ceremonial knife. The rite demands that every challenger leave a mark on their own arm before the duel, so that the desert recognises them. “Every mark will make you harder,” she says. “The sand says so, not I.”
en.choice.desert-rito.extra0.text: Idris is with you, silent, his steel arm uncovered: he has no scars to offer.
en.choice.desert-rito.extra1.text: On a dune, far off, a figure watches: you think you recognise Idris.
en.choice.desert-rito.a.label: You accept the rite: the mark is yours
en.choice.desert-rito.a.text: The cut is clean and brief. The pain turns into something hard that doesn't leave you: you already know it will stay forever.
en.choice.desert-rito.b.label: You ask for the rite to be public, before the caravan
en.choice.desert-rito.b.text: The Mummy hesitates, then nods. For the first time in centuries the rite has an audience. The travellers won't forget the scene, or your face.
en.choice.desert-rito.c.label: You refuse the rite and fight by your own rules
en.choice.desert-rito.c.text: The Mummy lowers the knife. “As you wish.” For a moment you feel the eyes of the entire temple on your skin, and it isn't a pleasant feeling.
en.choice.desert-lia.title: Lia in the storm
en.choice.desert-lia.text: The storm takes the shape of a giant. As you prepare, a figure crosses the sand with a recorder clutched to her chest: Lia Marek. She followed your name all the way here, on foot and by caravan. “I'm not interested in the ring any more,” she says. “I'm interested in who brought you here.”
en.choice.desert-lia.extra0.text: She trusts you: you treated her like a person, not a headline.
en.choice.desert-lia.extra1.text: She hasn't forgotten the six instead of the three. Yet here she is, and you still don't know if to forgive you or to expose you.
en.choice.desert-lia.a.label: You tell her about the Notary and the Registry: let everyone know
en.choice.desert-lia.a.text: Lia listens without breathing. When she leaves, her notebook holds a story someone will want silenced. Your name is in it, and not on the winners' side.
en.choice.desert-lia.b.label: You give her only the version that makes you great
en.choice.desert-lia.b.text: Lia writes. “A fine story,” she says, and it isn't clear if it's a compliment. The headline that follows will be the biggest you've ever had.
en.choice.desert-lia.c.label: You send her away: it's too dangerous for her
en.choice.desert-lia.c.text: Lia looks at you as if about to speak, then nods. She leaves at a brisk pace, and for a while you notice you feel less alone and less seen.
en.choice.desert-colosso.title: The giant that reassembles
en.choice.desert-colosso.text: The storm takes the shape of a giant. Resisting is useless: the Colossus collapses and rebuilds itself every time. Someone in the caravan says there is a way to face it, but it requires standing still while the sand rushes over you.
en.choice.desert-colosso.a.label: You face it openly on its own ground
en.choice.desert-colosso.a.text: Every blow is a wave, and you find yourself laughing through the pain. When it ends, the caravan has already stopped counting.
en.choice.desert-colosso.b.label: You wait for the storm to wear it down
en.choice.desert-colosso.b.text: You stay still under a tarp for two hours. When the wind drops, the Colossus is smaller and you are clearer: patience isn't cowardice.
en.choice.desert-colosso.c.label: You use the storm to vanish and strike by surprise
en.choice.desert-colosso.c.text: Nobody sees you enter or leave. Someone swears they saw the Colossus stumble on its own, and that isn't entirely false.
en.choice.desert-faraone.title: The Pharaoh's price
en.choice.desert-faraone.text: The pyramid shines like a second sun. From the throne, the Pharaoh looks down at you: “You crossed my realm without bowing. Whoever does not bow has a price or a reason. Tell me yours.”
en.choice.desert-faraone.extra0.text: Behind him, among the servants, you recognise Nuhra: she had time to tell them about you.
en.choice.desert-faraone.extra1.text: You have nothing in your pocket that ties you to any place. The Pharaoh notices, and smiles.
en.choice.desert-faraone.a.label: You bow: respect for his realm and his people
en.choice.desert-faraone.a.text: The Pharaoh did not expect the gesture and for a moment his marble expression slips. “Rare,” he says. “Respect is the luxury of the strong.”
en.choice.desert-faraone.b.label: You refuse: you bow only to those who taught you
en.choice.desert-faraone.b.text: The hall holds its breath. The Pharaoh laughs, and the sound rumbles like low thunder. “You have a teacher, then. I hope he is alive.”
en.choice.desert-faraone.b.lock: There is no teacher you feel bound to.
en.choice.desert-faraone.c.label: You propose a pact: his power in exchange for your service
en.choice.desert-faraone.c.text: The Pharaoh leans forward. “There it is, at last: a price.” You realise you are already thinking about how much you can take, not how much you will have to give.
en.choice.desert-faraone.c.lock: You don't yet hunger enough to propose a pact like that.
en.choice.ocean-relitto.title: The harbour of wrecks
en.choice.ocean-relitto.text: The harbour is a graveyard of ships. As you run along the planks toward the Armoured Shark, you spot a freshly sunk wreck with three sailors clinging to the mast. A smuggler on the next boat shouts: “The cargo's all mine, if you leave it to me!”
en.choice.ocean-relitto.extra0.text: One of the sailors wears a camp tag around his neck: he recognises you and greets you with a shout.
en.choice.ocean-relitto.extra1.text: One of the sailors wears a camp tag around his neck, and has your own way of avoiding eye contact.
en.choice.ocean-relitto.a.label: You save the sailors before thinking of the Shark
en.choice.ocean-relitto.a.text: You carry them one by one to the quay, waves biting at your ankles. The Shark waits, patient: now he is the one in a hurry.
en.choice.ocean-relitto.b.label: You take the cargo and let the sailors fend for themselves
en.choice.ocean-relitto.b.text: The cargo is heavy and worth a lot. Behind you, you hear the water, the voices, then nothing. You don't turn: it doesn't seem necessary.
en.choice.ocean-relitto.c.label: You carve your name on the wreck and move on
en.choice.ocean-relitto.c.text: For a moment you feel ridiculous. Then you see a fishing boat slow down to read it, and you realise it works.
en.choice.ocean-sirena.title: The song that remembers
en.choice.ocean-sirena.text: The Sonic Siren doesn't sing notes: she sings memories. Your bones vibrate and, among the waves, you recognise voices you haven't heard in months. She dares you to chase a sound faster than you.
en.choice.ocean-sirena.extra0.text: You hear Gorin's voice counting rounds aloud, softly, like at four in the morning in the gym.
en.choice.ocean-sirena.extra1.text: You search for Gorin's voice and find only silence. It weighs more than any note.
en.choice.ocean-sirena.extra2.text: Another voice, younger and rougher, repeats a piece of Idris's advice that you have already used.
en.choice.ocean-sirena.a.label: You listen to the end, without defending yourself
en.choice.ocean-sirena.a.text: The song ends and you remain kneeling on the planks. What you heard wasn't pleasant, but it's yours. You've understood what that name really means.
en.choice.ocean-sirena.b.label: You plug your ears and chase the sound on instinct alone
en.choice.ocean-sirena.b.text: You run into the void, hearing nothing. When you reach the Siren, she is the one surprised: nobody had ever ignored her song to charge her.
en.choice.ocean-sirena.c.label: You sing along, to let everyone hear you're there
en.choice.ocean-sirena.c.text: Your notes aren't beautiful, but they're loud. Passing fishermen stop to listen, laugh, applaud.
en.choice.ocean-nucleo.title: The pirate's core
en.choice.ocean-nucleo.text: On the deck of the flying ship, the Energy Pirate guards a core that pulses like a heart. “Whoever holds it tight has the storm in their hands,” he laughs. When he falls, the core rolls across the wood: everyone sees it and everyone wants it.
en.choice.ocean-nucleo.extra0.text: Idris is beside you, his steel arm outstretched. “Shall we split it?” he asks, and for once it doesn't sound like a front.
en.choice.ocean-nucleo.extra1.text: Idris appears out of the smoke, already in position. “It's mine,” he says, and it doesn't sound like a threat: it sounds like a plea for recognition.
en.choice.ocean-nucleo.a.label: You split the core into equal parts
en.choice.ocean-nucleo.a.text: It takes steady hands and some courage. When you finish, neither of you holds the whole storm. Both of you feel it.
en.choice.ocean-nucleo.b.label: You take it all: you need it more than anyone
en.choice.ocean-nucleo.b.text: The core fills you like a jolt. For a moment the ocean seems small. Then you look at where Idris is, and understand that you have chosen.
en.choice.ocean-nucleo.c.label: You throw it into the sea: nobody should have it
en.choice.ocean-nucleo.c.text: The core sinks, leaving a trail of light that fades in seconds. Someone curses you, someone stays silent. For a moment it's the only thing you're sure of.
en.choice.ocean-kraken.title: The crew in the tentacles
en.choice.ocean-kraken.text: The waves become arms. The Kraken has seized a merchant ship and the crew is still on deck. You have only seconds: strike the monster's eye to end the fight at once, or free the people first.
en.choice.ocean-kraken.extra0.text: Among the gunners you recognise the boy from the camp. He sees you and raises an arm: he hasn't forgotten.
en.choice.ocean-kraken.extra1.text: A gunner watches you from the rail. He says nothing, but there is a memory in his gaze that doesn't help him trust.
en.choice.ocean-kraken.a.label: You free the crew before anything else
en.choice.ocean-kraken.a.text: Three tentacles, a listing deck, a man handing you a child. When the Kraken turns, you are already in the middle of the fight, bare-handed and shorter of breath.
en.choice.ocean-kraken.b.label: You strike the Kraken's eye: whoever wins saves everyone
en.choice.ocean-kraken.b.text: The blow lands clean. The monster screams and lets go, and the deck settles. Nobody mentions what would have happened if you'd missed.
en.choice.ocean-kraken.c.label: You send the crew to the lifeboats and stay alone
en.choice.ocean-kraken.c.text: When they look back, they can't see you any more. Only the sound of water and your own breath remain: no witnesses, no applause.
en.choice.ocean-leviatano.title: The Leviathan's route
en.choice.ocean-leviatano.text: Beneath the surface something breathes like a mountain. An old navigator, Sael, joins you at the bow: “If you stop it, the route to the forest will be open. For anyone. Someone will have to decide who it belongs to.”
en.choice.ocean-leviatano.extra0.text: The light of the core you carry glows in the water, and Sael notices.
en.choice.ocean-leviatano.extra1.text: Sael looks at your chest, where the core pulses. “That isn't yours,” she says, but without anger.
en.choice.ocean-leviatano.a.label: You promise the route will stay free for everyone
en.choice.ocean-leviatano.a.text: Sael holds out her hand. “A promise is worth as much as the one who makes it,” she says. “I'll write it on the chart, beside your name.”
en.choice.ocean-leviatano.b.label: You claim the route as yours: whoever passes, pays
en.choice.ocean-leviatano.b.text: Sael shakes her head but doesn't stop you. For months, in taverns, your name and the word “toll” will share the same sentence.
en.choice.ocean-leviatano.b.lock: Nobody would pay a toll to an unknown name: you need more Fame.
en.choice.ocean-leviatano.c.label: You take the route in silence and tell no one
en.choice.ocean-leviatano.c.text: There is no glory, no deceit. Sael watches you vanish at the horizon as if she'd never met you, and it feels right that way.
en.choice.forest-frutteto.title: The orchard of the bite
en.choice.forest-frutteto.text: The forest begins where the sea ends, and the first tree you meet bears the same fruit you tasted out of curiosity months ago. Now there are hundreds, hanging like lanterns. A hermit, Oru, watches you from a branch: “Whoever eats two,” he says, “does not come back.”
en.choice.forest-frutteto.extra0.text: The pact with the Pharaoh weighs on your skin, like a second fruit already eaten.
en.choice.forest-frutteto.a.label: You eat another: you want to know how far it goes
en.choice.forest-frutteto.a.text: The taste is identical, but the body reacts before the mind: your fingers lengthen, your heartbeat quickens. Oru shakes his head, and there is pity in it.
en.choice.forest-frutteto.b.label: You gather a basket to resell
en.choice.forest-frutteto.b.text: The basket is heavy. You know how much they will pay for it, and you prefer not to think about who will eat it.
en.choice.forest-frutteto.c.label: You burn the orchard: nobody else should taste it
en.choice.forest-frutteto.c.text: Fire runs through the branches and the forest groans. Oru does not stop you. You understand that sometimes destroying is harder than taking.
en.choice.forest-visione.title: What you might become
en.choice.forest-visione.text: Among the trunks a voice whispers that knows you. The Forest Spirit shows you what you might become, and your wounds begin to close by themselves. The images change according to who you have been so far.
en.choice.forest-visione.extra0.text: You see yourself with a straight back and empty hands, standing among people who aren't afraid of you.
en.choice.forest-visione.extra1.text: You see yourself from behind, in the hurry of someone with something to hide.
en.choice.forest-visione.extra2.text: You see yourself in an arena roaring your name, wearing a face that is no longer your own.
en.choice.forest-visione.extra3.text: You see yourself in an empty room, free and without witnesses.
en.choice.forest-visione.extra4.text: You see yourself seated on a throne of ash, the hunger never gone.
en.choice.forest-visione.extra5.text: You see yourself at a window with a steaming cup: the world climbing, you staying.
en.choice.forest-visione.a.label: You embrace what you saw
en.choice.forest-visione.a.text: The Spirit smiles and your wounds close faster. The vision stops being a warning and becomes a promise.
en.choice.forest-visione.b.label: You reject it: you are more than a prophecy
en.choice.forest-visione.b.text: The image shatters like glass. The Spirit stays silent, then whispers: “Then choose every day.”
en.choice.forest-visione.c.label: You ask it to show you someone else's future
en.choice.forest-visione.c.text: You see an old man polishing a punching bag, a reporter writing, a man with a steel arm walking toward a light. You can't tell which are truths and which are wishes.
en.choice.forest-nomi.title: The Treant and the names
en.choice.forest-nomi.text: The ancient Treant holds no anger, only a patience thousands of years old. At its roots, carved into the bark, are names: hundreds, in many languages, some very fresh. “These are the ones who climbed,” it says in a voice slow as a season. “None has ever come down.”
en.choice.forest-nomi.extra0.text: Among the most recent names you recognise one carved with care: Idris, still without an end date.
en.choice.forest-nomi.extra1.text: Among the most recent names you recognise one carved in anger: Idris, with a line half struck through.
en.choice.forest-nomi.a.label: You carve your name beside the others
en.choice.forest-nomi.a.text: The bark opens slowly to receive it. The Treant says nothing, but somewhere in the woods a branch bends: a form of respect, or of compassion.
en.choice.forest-nomi.b.label: You plant a seed for those who never returned
en.choice.forest-nomi.b.text: The Treant gazes at you for a long time. “No one has done this in centuries,” it says. The seed sinks without a sound.
en.choice.forest-nomi.c.label: You scratch out a name: it didn't deserve to remain
en.choice.forest-nomi.c.text: The bark bleeds resin. Nobody stops you and nobody thanks you. You wonder whether you decided, or were allowed to decide.
en.choice.forest-cacciatore.title: The hunter and his daughter
en.choice.forest-cacciatore.text: Someone has been following you for days: he wants the power you carry, born of a fruit tasted out of curiosity. When the Fruit Hunter catches up with you, he draws no weapon. He sits on a log and says: “I have a daughter who is no longer a person. I want to know what was done to her.”
en.choice.forest-cacciatore.extra0.text: He looks at your hands: he has seen fingers that long too many times already.
en.choice.forest-cacciatore.extra1.text: He smells the burning on you, and for a moment anger leaves his eyes like relief.
en.choice.forest-cacciatore.a.label: You listen to his story and stay to help him
en.choice.forest-cacciatore.a.text: You spend the night telling him every detail, even the ones that hurt. By dawn he is no longer an enemy, nor a friend: he is someone who believed you.
en.choice.forest-cacciatore.b.label: You strike first: you can't afford doubt
en.choice.forest-cacciatore.b.text: He is fast, but you are faster. As he falls, he looks at you as though he had been waiting for exactly this.
en.choice.forest-cacciatore.c.label: You offer to carry the burden alongside him
en.choice.forest-cacciatore.c.text: He shakes his head but doesn't refuse. He will leave at dawn and, someday, perhaps return with an answer.
en.choice.forest-albero.title: The Tree's heart
en.choice.forest-albero.text: At the heart of the forest, roots as large as rivers grip the island. The World Tree doesn't speak: it watches you with a thousand leaf-eyes. You understand you can draw on its strength for as long as it lasts, or ask to borrow it.
en.choice.forest-albero.extra0.text: On a root, suddenly, a small new leaf sprouts: the one from the seed you planted.
en.choice.forest-albero.extra1.text: The roots around you are dark, and the bark you wounded hasn't stopped bleeding yet.
en.choice.forest-albero.a.label: You take its strength to the very end
en.choice.forest-albero.a.text: The Tree doesn't resist. For hours the woods around you wither slowly as you grow. When you leave, you no longer need to ask for anything.
en.choice.forest-albero.a.lock: You lack the hunger to tear the heart out of an entire forest.
en.choice.forest-albero.b.label: You borrow only what you need
en.choice.forest-albero.b.text: A leaf detaches and falls into your hands. Nothing else happens, but you feel something alive in your palm, and its weight feels right.
en.choice.forest-albero.c.label: You carve a mark on the roots so your passing is remembered
en.choice.forest-albero.c.text: The mark remains, small and sharp. Any traveller will see it, in the future, and wonder who it belongs to.
en.choice.volcano-notaio.title: The man in black, again
en.choice.volcano-notaio.text: The summit smokes and the sky has sunk low. The man in black waits for you on the path, now without his notebook. His face is more tired than you remembered. “This is where my trade ends,” he says, “and yours begins. Ask me anything you like.”
en.choice.volcano-notaio.extra0.text: On the cuff of his jacket you can still see the ink of your signature, like a stain that won't wash out.
en.choice.volcano-notaio.extra1.text: He looks at you the way one looks at something one could not buy, and so ended up respecting.
en.choice.volcano-notaio.extra2.text: The weight of the list under your jacket now feels like an answer.
en.choice.volcano-notaio.extra3.text: He knows about the list you burned. He doesn't say so, but moves his hand as if brushing something no longer there.
en.choice.volcano-notaio.a.label: You ask him the whole truth about the Registry
en.choice.volcano-notaio.a.text: “The Registry doesn't record winners,” he says. “It records those who are remembered, because Titans live on names. I have given many. Not all came out whole.” For the first time he doesn't look like a man in black: he looks like a man.
en.choice.volcano-notaio.b.label: You ask him to hand you his place
en.choice.volcano-notaio.b.text: The Notary smiles. “That's what I hoped you'd ask.” He hands you an inkless pen and a small key.
en.choice.volcano-notaio.c.label: You turn your back: from here you need only the mountain
en.choice.volcano-notaio.c.text: “Like all of them,” he murmurs. “And like none.” He doesn't follow, and the path climbs on its own.
en.choice.volcano-golem.title: The weary golem
en.choice.volcano-golem.text: The Lava Golem is weary of the world, and each step leaves a crack. When he sees you, he doesn't attack: he says, in a voice of breaking stone, that he only wants to rest. “But someone,” he adds, “must decide how it ends.”
en.choice.volcano-golem.extra0.text: Lia Marek has caught up with you once more, recorder on and shoes worn thin.
en.choice.volcano-golem.a.label: You promise that after the duel you'll let him rest
en.choice.volcano-golem.a.text: The Golem tilts his head. A crack glows red, almost a smile. “Then let us fight well.”
en.choice.volcano-golem.b.label: You force him to work for you: his forge is worth a fortune
en.choice.volcano-golem.b.text: The Golem doesn't protest. But when you look up, all his anger seems to have moved to a place you can't see.
en.choice.volcano-golem.c.label: You ask Lia to tell his story to the world
en.choice.volcano-golem.c.text: Lia writes all night, and the next morning the Golem is a voice, not just a walking mountain. Your name stands beside his.
en.choice.volcano-golem.c.lock: There is nobody who would tell a story like this.
en.choice.volcano-demone.title: The Demon's pact
en.choice.volcano-demone.text: The Blazing Demon recognises you: “You're the one who climbs.” He doesn't want to stop you: he wants to know how far you can go before you burn. He offers a power that is no gift but an advance, and you will pay for it later with a piece of who you are.
en.choice.volcano-demone.extra0.text: For an instant you think you hear, far away, the sound of a punching bag.
en.choice.volcano-demone.a.label: You accept: you need every spark
en.choice.volcano-demone.a.text: The fire runs through you and for a moment you are taller than the mountain. Then it leaves you with a void you cannot yet name.
en.choice.volcano-demone.b.label: You refuse: what you have is enough
en.choice.volcano-demone.b.text: The Demon laughs, a sound like burning wood. “Odd,” he says. “Almost everyone says no, then comes back.”
en.choice.volcano-demone.c.label: You ask in return that Gorin's gym never closes
en.choice.volcano-demone.c.text: The Demon hesitates, puzzled. “It isn't a power,” he says. “But I accept.” On the horizon a small, distant light flickers on.
en.choice.volcano-demone.c.lock: You have no gym to protect.
en.choice.volcano-idris.title: The companion and the rival
en.choice.volcano-idris.text: The sky darkens. The Cataclysmic Dragon spreads his wings and ash falls like rain. A silhouette climbs the path behind you with a stride you know: Idris. He isn't looking at the dragon. He is looking at you.
en.choice.volcano-idris.extra0.text: He hasn't come to stop you. He is out of breath and wears a new, rough smile.
en.choice.volcano-idris.extra1.text: His steel arm is outstretched, but not toward the dragon: toward you.
en.choice.volcano-idris.extra2.text: He is alone. He has the expression of someone who has always been preparing for this moment.
en.choice.volcano-idris.a.label: You hold out your hand: you face the dragon together
en.choice.volcano-idris.a.text: Idris hesitates. Then he grips hard, like someone who has waited years to be called by name. “Ten years ago I didn't know how,” he says.
en.choice.volcano-idris.a.lock: There is no bond left between you to appeal to.
en.choice.volcano-idris.b.label: You let him go first: if he falls, the road is yours
en.choice.volcano-idris.b.text: Idris runs ahead without turning. You realise you haven't lied to him, nor told him the truth.
en.choice.volcano-idris.c.label: You challenge him here and now to decide who climbs
en.choice.volcano-idris.c.text: Above you the dragon watches two people choose not to be allies. Whoever has more breath wins; time will judge the rest.
en.choice.volcano-titano.title: The Titan
en.choice.volcano-titano.text: At the crater's summit the Titan awaits you, born from the heart of the world. Behind you, the sea and every face you've met. “Your journey ends here,” he says, “or truly begins. Tell me what you want, and fire will decide the rest.”
en.choice.volcano-titano.extra0.text: Among the faces, one holds your gaze: an old man with the wraps still in his hands.
en.choice.volcano-titano.extra1.text: Idris stands beside you, panting, and isn't looking at the Titan: he looks where you look.
en.choice.volcano-titano.extra2.text: Somewhere, in a distant newsroom, a story is already printed and waiting only to be read.
en.choice.volcano-titano.extra3.text: In your pocket, the Notary's key weighs like a promise.
en.choice.volcano-titano.extra4.text: The void the Demon left opens like a door demanding to be crossed.
en.choice.volcano-titano.a.label: You take his place
en.choice.volcano-titano.a.text: The Titan bows and hands you the fire. For a moment it seems the most natural thing in the world.
en.choice.volcano-titano.a.lock: You don't hunger enough to bear a throne like that.
en.choice.volcano-titano.b.label: You break the Registry, once and for all
en.choice.volcano-titano.b.text: The Titan looks at you for a long while. “No one has ever asked it in that voice.” A crack runs across every page the world has written about you.
en.choice.volcano-titano.b.lock: To break an ancient pact you need a word nobody can dispute: you need more Honor.
en.choice.volcano-titano.c.label: You let your name go beyond you
en.choice.volcano-titano.c.text: “It will be greater than you,” says the Titan. “Do you know that?” You say yes, and the mountain seems to nod.
en.choice.volcano-titano.c.lock: It needs a name the world already knows: you need more Fame.
en.choice.volcano-titano.d.label: You simply face him, asking nothing of anyone
en.choice.volcano-titano.d.text: The Titan smiles as rock smiles when it meets water. “Then begin.” It isn't the grandest choice: it is yours.
en.epilogue.throne.title: The throne of ash
en.epilogue.throne.text: The fire welcomes you without asking permission. When you open your eyes, the mountain breathes at your rhythm, the sea is a carpet at your feet and the Registry is a book waiting to be filled. You have won: it is the simplest word you know, and from today nobody can tell you otherwise. At the foot of the volcano a man in black closes a notebook and smiles. Your name is on the first page: it no longer needs anyone to write it.
en.epilogue.throne.extra0.text: The Notary's key opens a door you didn't know you had: the entire archive, with every name your predecessor consumed. Now they are yours.
en.epilogue.throne.extra1.text: Back home, the gym is closed. Nobody will ever tell you, and you will never ask.
en.epilogue.throne.extra2.text: Idris never reached the top. Nobody speaks of it. Sometimes you still hear him running ahead.
en.epilogue.throne.extra3.text: Gorin writes you a single line, months later: “The knee?” You don't know how to answer, and you don't.
en.epilogue.break.title: The Registry broken
en.epilogue.break.text: The first crack runs across the stone and reaches the sea. For an instant the whole world holds its breath; then the pages of the Registry detach from the sky like light ash, each one carrying a name. Somewhere in the world someone wakes up feeling they have started breathing again. You walk down the mountain on foot, without throne, without title, with empty hands. For the first time in a long while nobody is watching you, and you don't mind.
en.epilogue.break.extra0.text: Idris walks down with you. He doesn't speak, but now and then his steel arm brushes your shoulder, as if to remind you he is there.
en.epilogue.break.extra1.text: Lia Marek publishes the story. The next day the Notary has nowhere left to stand.
en.epilogue.break.extra2.text: Gorin's gym reopens the following month. On the wall, the photo turned backwards is set straight again.
en.epilogue.break.extra3.text: When you reach the gym, Gorin says nothing. He hands you the wraps, and you tie them on like the first time.
en.epilogue.break.extra4.text: The Lava Golem finally rests, and his story is in the hands of anyone willing to read it.
en.epilogue.legend.title: The name beyond the man
en.epilogue.legend.text: The Titan neither kills nor bows you: he lets you go with a single sentence, which the wind carries everywhere. In harbours, gyms, desert caravans, the story of the one who climbed from the ring to the volcano begins to circulate in a thousand versions. In some you are a hero, in others a fraud; in all of them, unmistakably, you. At times, in the mirror, you look for the face they talk about and can't find it. But your name keeps walking without you, and no one can stop it now.
en.epilogue.legend.extra0.text: Lia Marek writes your biography. The version everyone will remember is almost true, and that is why it works.
en.epilogue.legend.extra1.text: Lia writes your biography and the six rounds stay six. Someone corrects it now and then: nobody reads the correction.
en.epilogue.legend.extra2.text: In the taverns your name stays tied to a toll. Some pay it proudly, some with resentment.
en.epilogue.legend.extra3.text: On the fishermen's charts, beside the route to the forest, someone has written your name and a single word: “free”.
en.epilogue.legend.extra4.text: At the roots of the Treant your name has stopped being the last.
en.epilogue.fighter.title: The journey continues
en.epilogue.fighter.text: The Titan looks at you for a long while, then lowers his arms and the crater calms. You didn't take his place and you broke nothing: you crossed the mountain and kept walking. Behind you remain a sea, a desert, a forest, a summit and a notebook someone, somewhere, is still writing. Ahead of you lies neither throne nor fall: a road without a name. It is the first time it truly belongs to you.
en.epilogue.fighter.extra0.text: In a suburban gym, an old man hangs a photo at the back of a wall and never turns it around again.
en.epilogue.fighter.extra1.text: On a ship, a man with a steel arm gazes at the horizon and for the first time doesn't see a debt there.
en.epilogue.fighter.extra2.text: Your name precedes you everywhere, but you decide where to go.
en.epilogue.fighter.extra3.text: The hunger hasn't gone, but now you know it: you steer it, it doesn't steer you.
en.epilogue.fighter.extra4.text: Nobody ever doubted your word, and nobody is going to start now.
en.epilogue.fighter.extra5.text: Sometimes stopping is the most ambitious thing there is.
en.virtue.honor.name: Honor
en.virtue.honor.desc: Keeping your word, respecting your opponent, loyalty to those who trained you.
en.virtue.honor.perk0.text: Dirty tricks: the foe starts with 6% less HP, but nobody pays you gladly (−10% gold from victories).
en.virtue.honor.perk3.text: Steady guard: you start each duel with 4 block.
en.virtue.honor.perk4.text: Unshakable guard: you start each duel with 8 block.
en.virtue.fame.name: Fame
en.virtue.fame.desc: How much the world talks about you: crowds, reporters and enemies who already know who you are.
en.virtue.fame.perk0.text: Shadow: nobody knows you and foes underestimate you. You draw +1 card on the first turn.
en.virtue.fame.perk3.text: Celebrity: crowds pay to watch you. +10% gold from victories.
en.virtue.fame.perk4.text: Legend: wherever you go, they are waiting for you. +25% gold from victories.
en.virtue.ambition.name: Ambition
en.virtue.ambition.desc: The hunger to climb ever higher, whatever the price.
en.virtue.ambition.perk0.text: Content: no hurry, no risk. You start each duel with 3 block.
en.virtue.ambition.perk3.text: Hungry: +1 energy on the first turn.
en.virtue.ambition.perk4.text: Insatiable: +1 energy and +1 card on the first turn, but you start with 4 less HP.

epilogues.title: Il trono di cenere
epilogues.text: Il fuoco ti accoglie senza chiederti il permesso. Quando riapri gli occhi, la montagna respira al tuo ritmo, il mare è un tappeto ai tuoi piedi e il Registro è un libro che aspetta di essere riempito. Hai vinto: è la parola più semplice che conosci, e da oggi nessuno potrà dirti il contrario. Alla base del vulcano un uomo in nero chiude un taccuino e sorride. Il tuo nome è in prima pagina: non ha più bisogno di essere scritto da nessuno.

extra.text: La chiave del Notaio apre una porta che non sapevi di avere: l'archivio intero, con tutti i nomi che il tuo predecessore ha consumato. Adesso sono tuoi.
A casa, la palestra è chiusa. Nessuno te lo dirà mai, e tu non lo chiederai.
Idris non è arrivato in cima. Nessuno ne parla. Tu, a volte, lo senti ancora correre in avanti.
Gorin ti scrive una sola riga, qualche mese dopo: «Il ginocchio?» Non sai come rispondere, e non rispondi.

epilogues.title: Il Registro spezzato
epilogues.text: La prima incrinatura corre sulla pietra e arriva fino al mare. Per un istante tutto il mondo trattiene il fiato; poi le pagine del Registro si staccano dal cielo come cenere leggera, e ognuna porta un nome. Qualcuno si risveglia, in qualche parte del mondo, con la sensazione di aver ripreso a respirare. Tu scendi dalla montagna a piedi, senza trono, senza titolo, con le mani vuote. Per la prima volta da molto tempo nessuno ti sta guardando, e non ti dispiace.

extra.text: Idris scende con te. Non parla, ma ogni tanto il braccio d'acciaio ti sfiora la spalla, come per ricordarti che c'è.
Lia Marek pubblica la storia. Il giorno dopo il Notaio non ha più un posto dove stare.
La palestra di Gorin riapre il mese dopo. Sul muro, la foto girata al contrario viene rimessa dritta.
Quando arrivi alla palestra, Gorin non dice niente. Ti porge le fasce, e tu le allacci come la prima volta.
Il Golem di lava riposa, finalmente, e la sua storia è nelle mani di chiunque voglia leggerla.

epilogues.title: Il nome oltre l'uomo
epilogues.text: Il Titano non ti uccide e non ti inchina: ti lascia andare con una frase sola, che il vento porta ovunque. Nei porti, nelle palestre, nelle carovane del deserto, la storia di chi è salito dal ring al vulcano comincia a circolare con mille varianti. In alcune sei un eroe, in altre un truffatore; in tutte, inconfondibilmente, sei tu. A volte, allo specchio, cerchi il volto di cui parlano e non lo trovi. Ma il tuo nome continua a camminare senza di te, e nessuno potrà più fermarlo.

extra.text: Lia Marek scrive la tua biografia. La versione che tutti ricorderanno è quasi vera, e per questo funziona.
Lia scrive la tua biografia e i sei round restano sei. Qualcuno, a volte, la corregge: nessuno legge la correzione.
Nelle taverne il tuo nome resta legato a un pedaggio. Qualcuno lo paga con fierezza, qualcuno con rancore.
Sulle mappe dei pescatori, accanto alla rotta verso la foresta, qualcuno ha scritto il tuo nome e una sola parola: «libera».
Alle radici del Treant il tuo nome ha smesso di essere l'ultimo.

epilogues.title: Il viaggio che continua
epilogues.text: Il Titano ti guarda a lungo, poi abbassa le braccia e il cratere si placa. Non hai preso il suo posto e non hai spezzato niente: hai attraversato la montagna e hai continuato a camminare. Dietro di te restano un mare, un deserto, una foresta, una cima e un taccuino che qualcuno, da qualche parte, scrive ancora. Davanti a te non c'è né un trono né una caduta: c'è una strada senza nome. È la prima volta che ti appartiene davvero.

extra.text: In una palestra di periferia, un vecchio appende una foto in fondo a una parete e non la gira più.
Su una nave, un uomo con un braccio d'acciaio guarda l'orizzonte e per la prima volta non ci vede un debito.
Il tuo nome ti precede ovunque, ma sei tu a decidere dove andare.
La fame non è passata, ma ora la conosci: la guidi, non ti guida.
Nessuno ha mai dubitato della tua parola, e nessuno inizierà adesso.
A volte fermarsi è la cosa più ambiziosa che esista.
